instruction.text: Select the extra information which has been added to the sentence.

end.text: Brackets can be used when the extra information should stand out. They can come with their own extra punctuation, like an exclamation mark.

atoms.b: I am going on holiday next week (((to a tropical island!))) and I’m so excited.

instruction.text: Select the extra information which has been added to the sentence.

end.text: Commas can be used to include extra information in more formal writing. They should only be used if there are not already too many commas used in the sentence.

atoms.b: Steven, ((who normally cycles)), had to take the bus into work because of the weather.

instruction.text: Select the extra information which has been added to the sentence.

end.text: Dashes can be used in more informal, chatty writing.

atoms.b: She told me – ((I kid you not)) – she won the lottery.

atoms.a: My brother, who is taller than me, always beats me at tennis.
Whenever it rains (I always get) muddy.
Cricket – especially in the summer – is my favourite sport to play.

atoms.a: My friend Jack, who can be quite clumsy, spilled hot chocolate on his computer.
b: ++My friend Jack, who can be quite clumsy, spilled hot chocolate on his computer.
